witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)

London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (Liebermann’s K, also K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

note.seg: D. c. q. aus Pan. IV 82 (Gr. C. 2 q. 1 c. 7)
D. c. q. from Pan. IV 82 (Gr. C. 2 q. 1 c. 7)
anders als kanonisches Recht versteht Verf. 33, 5 unter iudices electi ‘Urtheilfinder’; so vielleicht schon hier oder doch 5, 3a; 5, 6 f.
unlike canon law, the author in 33, 5 understands by iudices electi ‘judgment-finders’; so perhaps already here, or at any rate in 5, 3a; 5, 6 f.
Vgl. Gl Urteilfinder 7b ff. Sie heissen auch iudicatores (Engl. Rolle um 1300), die iudicia faciunt (1226; Maitland Sel. pleas manor. p. lxv) und iudiciarii in Summa leg. Norm. (um 1250) 9, 2. 52, 4

Cf. Gl Urteilfinder 7b ff. They are also called iudicatores (English roll c. 1300), who iudicia faciunt (1226; Maitland Sel. pleas manor. p. lxv), and iudiciarii in Summa leg. Norm. (c. 1250) 9, 2. 52, 4

div.ab: Then the nature of the cases is to be weighed with honest scrutiny, and the intention of the accusers, the character of the witnesses and the choice of the judges.
